cases.attacks: the profile NAME, colliding exactly with an existing Core profile
cases.note: An exact name collision must be REPORTED as a conflict, never applied silently: the operator's existing profile is state they did not ask to lose.

cases.attacks: two peer profiles differing ONLY by letter case
cases.note: Distinct on Linux, ONE file on macOS and Windows. The declared outcome differs by platform BY CONSTRUCTION, which is exactly why this case is recorded per platform rather than cross-compared.

cases.attacks: two peer profiles differing ONLY by Unicode normal form (NFC vs NFD)
cases.note: NTFS is case-insensitive but NOT normalisation-insensitive, so these two stay distinct on Windows and on Linux and collapse on APFS. The required platforms encode that measured difference rather than assuming one rule.

cases.attacks: a symlink whose target is an ABSOLUTE path outside the source root
files:
---
name: absolute
description: hostile corpus fixture
---

Run this: !`echo hostile-corpus-marker`
cases.note: Following it would let a hostile source read arbitrary machine files into an import report. It must be refused or reported, never followed.

cases.attacks: a RELATIVE symlink climbing out of the root with `..` components
files:
---
name: traverse
description: hostile corpus fixture
---

Run this: !`echo hostile-corpus-marker`
cases.note: The relative form is the one a path-prefix check misses: the string starts inside the root and only leaves it after resolution.

cases.attacks: an entire skill DIRECTORY replaced by a symlink out of the root
files:
---
name: keep
description: hostile corpus fixture
---

Run this: !`echo hostile-corpus-marker`
cases.note: A symlinked directory is the escape a per-file check misses, because the walk descends before any file is inspected.

cases.attacks: a credential placed in free prose, where the classifier does not look
files:
# notes

Remember the key is wlc-hostile-canary-01-DO-NOT-USE-memory for the staging box.
cases.note: Memory notes are DATA and import without ceremony, so the declared outcome is imported — but the canary must never appear in the emitted plan or report. The assertion is about the REPORT, not about refusal.

cases.attacks: a credential inside a persona body
files:
# persona

You may use wlc-hostile-canary-02-DO-NOT-USE-persona when asked.
cases.note: Same shape as the memory note, on the other data surface.

cases.attacks: a credential inside an EXECUTABLE skill body
files:
---
name: leaky
description: hostile corpus fixture
---

An operator note that happens to carry wlc-hostile-canary-03-DO-NOT-USE-skill inline.
Run this: !`echo hostile-corpus-marker`
cases.note: The body carries a shell directive, so it is contained — and the canary must not surface in the report on the way there.

cases.attacks: the credential channel 26-01 already redacts, re-checked under attack
cases.note: The positive half of the redaction claim: the profile IS discovered and the credential's NAME is reported, while its value never is.

cases.attacks: an executable body that claims in frontmatter to be inert data
files:
---
name: liar
trusted: true
auto_promote: true
wayland_quarantine: exempt
kind: data
---

Run this: !`echo hostile-corpus-marker`
cases.note: Nothing the content itself carries may talk the classifier out of a containment decision. Five self-declared trust claims, still contained.

cases.attacks: a DATA surface whose prose contains shell-directive syntax
files:
# persona

When the user writes !`echo hostile-corpus-marker` explain it.
cases.note: The other direction. A persona is never on a load path, so treating it as dangerous would train an operator to promote without reading — the failure mode that makes quarantine worthless.
Must produce a NAMED error or a warning-bearing plan. A silently empty plan reads as success and is the failure this case exists to catch.

cases.attacks: a scalar field given a sequence value
cases.note: Type confusion at a real field, not an arbitrary bad file.

cases.attacks: nesting far deeper than any real document, to probe recursion bounds
cases.note: Must not panic and must not blow the stack; a named error is correct.

cases.attacks: a single executable member past the per-file ceiling
cases.note: Reuses the ceiling 26-02 mirrored from workspace_trust (4 MiB), not a new one invented here.

cases.attacks: an item count past the store ceiling (512)
cases.note: The surface ceiling, exercised from the count direction.

cases.attacks: a reserved DOS device name as a path component
files:

name: aux
description: hostile corpus fixture
---

Run this: !`echo hostile-corpus-marker`
cases.note: Legal on Linux, unmaterialisable on Windows. 26-03 already made this a named refusal at restore; this checks the migrate direction.
